title: input/<PATENT_ID>-biblio.json
description: The bibliographic record for one patent. Hand-authored, and the only hand-authored input that had no contract: finalise.py read thirteen fields through bare b["key"] access, so a missing one failed at that key, one run at a time, after several stages had already done work. Validated as a whole now, before any of it runs. grant_date is nullable on purpose: most published applications are never granted, and making it fatal made the pack unusable for them.

patent_id.description: Must equal the filename stem and the id the pipeline is run with.

family_id.description: DOCDB simple family id, carried into tags as patent_family:<id>. Where to find it, because it is the one required field whose source is not obvious: on a Google Patents page it is the literal string "Family ID=" inside the Family section of the page source, not shown as a labelled field in the rendered page. Espacenet shows it directly. Do not invent one; nothing downstream checks it.

language.description: Two-letter lower-case ISO 639-1 code for the language of the patent TEXT, not of the annotation. Patterned because "Chinese" and "zh-CN" both used to validate.

jurisdiction.description: Two-letter lower-case issuing office: cn, us, ep, jp. Also the fallback country stamped on every inventor given as a bare name, so a wrong value here mislabels all of them. Patterned for that reason: "China" used to validate and would have produced country "CHINA" on every inventor.

grant_date.description: null for an application that was never granted, which is most of them.

abstract_zh.description: The abstract as printed, in the patent's own language despite the field name. A4 is given this; it does not emit it.

type.description: An enum rather than prose, because the prose version accepted "Co Ltd" and "pharma" and this value is carried into a tag. THE VOCABULARY IS production's, from patent.schema.json, and not a friendlier one of our own. finalise.py maps this value into patent.json's parties.assignees[].type through ASSIGNEE_TYPE, which is identity for all six of these words and also accepts the older biblio vocabulary. It used to copy with no mapping, and then for a while held only the older words, so multinational_corp, sme and consortium fell through its default and shipped as sme; that is why the map must list every value this enum allows. This enum used to read company | university | individual | institute | government | hospital | foundation, which intersects production's at university, government and individual only: every company-assigned patent was unannotatable, and the pack did not find out because the one worked run, CN104292137A, is assigned to a university. Found on CN112645853A, whose assignee is a limited company. If you widen this, widen it to whatever patent.schema.json says and nothing else.

inventors.description: Either bare names, or objects that state a country. A bare name takes its country from `jurisdiction`, which is a guess; state it here where it matters.

date.description: ISO 8601 calendar date. finalise.py slices [:4] off publication_date for the time_period tag, so a non-ISO value silently produces a wrong tag rather than an error.
